speaker: Aron
text: Okay, let's get started. This is the weekly LandMARC sync. We've got Devin, Mackenzie and Curt in the room, and Colin said he'd join late. Matt T. sends his apologies, he's in the field this week.

speaker: Devin
text: Morning. I can kick off with the ILI update if that works.

speaker: Aron
text: Go for it.

speaker: Devin
text: So we received the new ILI deliverable for the Pembina line on Friday. It's a combo run, MFL plus IMU, so we have both the metal loss and the inertial data in one package. I've loaded it into the staging database and started the r2r alignment against the previous run.

speaker: Mackenzie
text: Which previous run are you aligning to? The twenty nineteen MFL or the twenty twenty one IMU-only run?

speaker: Devin
text: Both, actually. The r2r for metal loss uses the twenty nineteen MFL, and the r2r for bending strain uses the twenty twenty one IMU run. The girth weld matching is the backbone for both, so I align on girth welds first and then interpolate the chainage between them.

speaker: Curt
text: How good is the girth weld match rate so far?

speaker: Devin
text: About ninety seven percent on the first pass. The misses cluster around KP 87+200, where there was a reroute and a bunch of new girth welds went in. I'll need to handle that section by hand.

speaker: Aron
text: That reroute was the one BGC looked at, right? The geohazard near the river crossing?

speaker: Mackenzie
text: Yes. BGC classified it as a moderate geohazard, slow moving slope, and it's in our Watermarc layer as a watercourse crossing as well. So it shows up twice in LandMARC, once as a geohazard and once as a Watermarc crossing.

speaker: Aron
text: Okay. Let's make sure those two records are linked in LandMARC so nobody double counts them.

speaker: Mackenzie
text: Will do. I'll add a note in the Watermarc crossing record pointing to the geohazard ID.

speaker: Curt
text: Can I jump in on the bending strain side? I've been looking at the IMU results around KP 123+450.

speaker: Aron
text: Please.

speaker: Curt
text: There's a bending strain feature at KP 123+450 that's grown since the last IMU run. The incremental bending strain is about zero point one five percent, which is above our screening threshold. It sits right next to a girth weld, so that's the combination we care about: strain demand at a girth weld on a slope.

speaker: Devin
text: Is that in the BGC inventory?

speaker: Curt
text: It is. BGC has it as a geohazard site, a shallow translational slide. They recommended monitoring, and the IMU result kind of confirms the slope is still moving.

speaker: Aron
text: So that's a candidate for the Enbridge conversation as well. Enbridge asked us last month how we prioritise strain features at girth welds.

speaker: Mackenzie
text: Right, and the Pembina folks asked the same thing. I think we should write it up once and share it with both, with the client names stripped where needed.

speaker: Aron
text: Agreed. Curt, can you own the write-up on the KP 123+450 feature?

speaker: Curt
text: Yes, I'll draft it this week. I'll include the IMU bending strain profile, the girth weld details, the chainage, and the BGC geohazard assessment.

speaker: Devin
text: One thing on chainage. The ILI vendor reports odometer distance, and our LandMARC centreline uses chainage from the as-built survey. Those drift apart by up to thirty metres in a few places. So when Curt quotes KP 123+450, we should say which reference it's in.

speaker: Curt
text: Good point. I'll quote it in LandMARC chainage and give the ILI odometer distance in brackets.

speaker: Aron
text: Let's make that the rule for everything we send out. LandMARC chainage first, ILI distance second.

speaker: Mackenzie
text: I'll add that to the reporting template.

speaker: Aron
text: Okay, next item. Cambio side. Colin isn't on yet, so I'll cover it. On the Cambio side we've finished the data model changes for the IMU tables. The new schema stores bending strain per girth weld segment, so the r2r comparison can run directly in the database rather than in spreadsheets.

speaker: Devin
text: That would save me a day per run. Right now the r2r is half in Python and half in Excel.

speaker: Aron
text: That's the idea. Matt T. built the first version of the loader before he went to the field. Devin, can you test it against the Pembina ILI data this week?

speaker: Devin
text: Sure. I'll run the loader on the new ILI and the twenty twenty one IMU, then do the r2r in the database and compare against my spreadsheet numbers.

speaker: Mackenzie
text: While we're on Cambio, the Watermarc team asked whether LandMARC can push crossing updates to them automatically. At the moment they get a monthly export.

speaker: Aron
text: Possible, but let's not promise anything until Colin has looked at it. He owns the integration between LandMARC and Watermarc.

speaker: Curt
text: Speaking of Colin, I think he just joined.

speaker: Colin
text: Hi all, sorry I'm late. Car trouble. What did I miss?

speaker: Aron
text: No problem. Quick summary: Devin is doing the r2r on the new Pembina ILI, Curt is writing up the bending strain feature at KP 123+450, and Mackenzie is linking the BGC geohazard and Watermarc records in LandMARC. The open question for you is whether LandMARC can push crossing updates to Watermarc automatically.

speaker: Colin
text: It can, technically. The Watermarc API accepts updates, we just never turned it on. I'd want to test it on a copy first, and I'd want Matt T. to review the mapping since he wrote the original export.

speaker: Aron
text: Fine. Can you give us an estimate next week?

speaker: Colin
text: Yes, next Monday.

speaker: Mackenzie
text: One more geohazard item. BGC sent their updated inventory yesterday. There are four new sites, two of them on the Enbridge corridor and two on Pembina. One of the Pembina sites is near KP 140+015.

speaker: Devin
text: Is there an MFL or IMU feature near KP 140+015?

speaker: Mackenzie
text: Not that I could see. There's a girth weld anomaly flagged by the ILI vendor, but it's a geometry call, not metal loss, and nothing on bending strain.

speaker: Curt
text: I'd still overlay the IMU profile there. Sometimes the strain signal is small but the trend between runs is what matters. That's the whole point of the r2r.

speaker: Aron
text: Agreed. Devin, add KP 140+015 to the r2r review list.

speaker: Devin
text: Done. So the r2r review list is KP 87+200, KP 123+450, and KP 140+015.

speaker: Aron
text: Good. Next, the EMAT question. Enbridge asked whether we would use EMAT data if they ran it on the crack-susceptible sections.

speaker: Curt
text: We could, but LandMARC doesn't have a crack table yet. I'd treat EMAT as a separate layer for now and not try to align it with the MFL and IMU r2r.

speaker: Colin
text: I can add an EMAT table to the Cambio schema without too much trouble. Same pattern as the IMU tables: feature, girth weld reference, chainage, run ID.

speaker: Aron
text: Let's put that on the backlog but not this sprint. Our priority is the Pembina ILI and the BGC geohazard update.

speaker: Mackenzie
text: Quick question on the DoC. Do we have the signed DoC from the ILI vendor for the new run? Pembina will ask for it.

speaker: Devin
text: I have it. It came with the deliverable. I'll put it in the LandMARC document store next to the ILI report.

speaker: Curt
text: Before action items, can we talk about the dig program? Pembina wants to know which ILI features we'd recommend for excavation this season.

speaker: Devin
text: From the MFL side, there are three metal loss features above the reporting threshold, all on the Pembina line. None of them are near a girth weld, and none are in a BGC geohazard area, so they're straightforward.

speaker: Curt
text: From the IMU side, the only one I'd push for is KP 123+450. The bending strain at that girth weld is the thing that keeps me up at night. If we dig there, I'd want strain gauges installed so we can watch the slope after the backfill.

speaker: Mackenzie
text: BGC would support that. Their report says instrumentation is the preferred option over a slope stabilisation project until we know the rate of movement.

speaker: Colin
text: If we install gauges, I'd like the readings to go straight into LandMARC rather than a separate system. We could store them against the girth weld and the chainage, the same way we store the IMU results.

speaker: Aron
text: That makes sense. Let's include that in the recommendation to Pembina. Mackenzie, could you check whether Enbridge has done anything similar? I remember Matt T. mentioning an Enbridge site with gauges on a girth weld near a river crossing.

speaker: Mackenzie
text: I'll ask Matt T. when he's back from the field. I think it was in the Watermarc data too, since it was a watercourse crossing.

speaker: Devin
text: One last data quality note. The ILI vendor's IMU data has a gap of about two hundred metres near KP 87+200, where the tool lost its odometer wheel contact. That's the reroute section again. So the r2r for bending strain will have a hole there, and we should say so in the report.

speaker: Curt
text: Noted. I'll mention the gap and flag that the geohazard at KP 87+200 can't be assessed from IMU this run.

speaker: Aron
text: Great. Let's do action items. Devin: r2r on the new Pembina ILI, test Matt T.'s loader, add KP 140+015 to the review list, and upload the DoC. Curt: write up the bending strain feature at KP 123+450 with chainage and the BGC geohazard assessment. Mackenzie: link the geohazard and Watermarc records in LandMARC and update the reporting template. Colin: estimate for the LandMARC to Watermarc push, and an EMAT table design for the backlog.

speaker: Colin
text: And I'll loop in Matt T. on the mapping.

speaker: Aron
text: Perfect. And I'll draft the note to Enbridge and Pembina on how we prioritise bending strain at girth welds once Curt's write-up is done. Anything else?

speaker: Curt
text: Just that the BGC site visit is pencilled in for the twenty second. Mackenzie and I are going.

speaker: Mackenzie
text: Yes, and Devin, if you can get the r2r results for KP 123+450 to us before then, we can check the slope against the IMU data on site.

speaker: Devin
text: I'll aim for the twentieth.

speaker: Aron
text: Great. Thanks everyone. Same time next week.
